# ===========================================================================
# packages.txt - packages to bundle for the offline Ubuntu 26.04 desktop
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# One entry per line. Blank lines and everything after "#" are ignored, so
# inline comments are fine.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# LINE SYNTAX
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#   vlc                          a normal apt package (the default)
#   vlc=3.0.21-1build1           pinned to an exact version
#   apt:vlc                      the same as plain "vlc", written explicitly
#
#   https://host/path/x.deb      download this .deb AND resolve+download
#                                everything it depends on
#   url:https://host/get?fmt=deb same, for URLs that do not end in .deb
#
#   ./local-debs/zoom.deb        a .deb you already downloaded by hand; its
#   /abs/path/x.deb              dependencies are resolved and downloaded too
#   file:some/path.deb           the same, written explicitly
#
# Relative paths are resolved against the folder holding this file. Anything
# you drop in ./local-debs/ next to this file is picked up automatically - you
# do not have to list it. That is the easy way to feed the vendor .deb files
# listed in the "not in apt" blocks below into the bundle, dependencies and all.
#
# Examples (uncomment to use):
#   https://dl.google.com/linux/direct/google-chrome-stable_current_amd64.deb
#   url:https://discord.com/api/download?platform=linux&format=deb
#   ./local-debs/code_amd64.deb
#
# SIZE WARNING: the full active list resolves to roughly 12-20 GB of .deb files
# once dependencies and Recommends are pulled in. Trim the sections you do not
# need, or build with --no-recommends to cut it down substantially.
#
# VALIDATE THE LIST FIRST (on an online machine, before building the bundle):
#     apt-get install --dry-run -qq $(sed 's/#.*//' packages.txt | awk 'NF{print $1}') \
#         2>&1 | grep -i "unable to locate"
# apt aborts on the first unknown name, so removing typos up front saves a
# wasted download run.
#
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# EVERY SECTION ENDS WITH A "not in apt" BLOCK
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Those are commented pointers to software that is NOT in the Ubuntu archive.
# Marked by how the vendor ships it:
#     repo      an apt repository  <- ALWAYS PREFER THIS
#     deb       a standalone .deb file you download by hand
#     App       an AppImage: one executable, just copy it to the target
#     tgz/zip   an archive to unpack by hand
#     sh/run    a vendor installer script
#
# For a vendor REPO: add it to the OFFLINE machine's /etc/apt/sources.list.d/,
# re-run snapshot-target.sh, and the normal flow resolves its dependencies for
# you. This is by far the best option.
#
# For a standalone .deb:
#     1. build the bundle:  ./download-packages.sh --state target-state.tar.gz
#     2. drop the .deb files into  offline-bundle/debs/
#     3. re-run the exact same command - it re-indexes debs/ and picks them up
#     4. on the target:     sudo ./install-offline.sh --all
#   A loose .deb's dependencies are NOT resolved for you. If apt reports one
#   missing, add that name to this file and rebuild the bundle.
#
# Direct download URLs move around; where a URL looks fragile the vendor's
# download page is given instead. Verify checksums/signatures where offered.
#
# See the very bottom for packages that DOWNLOAD during install and therefore
# FAIL on an offline machine.
# ===========================================================================

# ===========================================================================
# SNAP-ONLY ON UBUNTU
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# For these the archive "deb" is only a shim that installs a snap, so it cannot
# work in an offline apt bundle:
#   firefox, chromium-browser, thunderbird, lxd, snap-store,
#   and most of Canonical's newer desktop apps.
#
# To carry a snap across offline:
#     online:   snap download <name>
#               -> produces <name>.snap and <name>.assert
#     offline:  sudo snap ack <name>.assert
#               sudo snap install <name>.snap
# Snap dependencies (bases like core22/core24, plus gnome-* content snaps) must
# be downloaded and acked the same way, BEFORE the app snap itself.
# ===========================================================================


# ===========================================================================
# DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED - these DOWNLOAD during installation and will FAIL
# on an offline machine even though the .deb itself installs fine:
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
#   ubuntu-restricted-extras   pulls ttf-mscorefonts-installer, which fetches
#                              the fonts from sourceforge in its postinst.
#                              "ubuntu-restricted-addons" (in the codecs
#                              section above) is the safe subset.
#   ttf-mscorefonts-installer  same reason
#   libdvd-pkg                 downloads and compiles the libdvdcss source
#   torbrowser-launcher        downloads the browser bundle on first run
#   steam-installer            downloads the Steam client on first run
#   flashplugin-installer      downloads from Adobe (and is dead anyway)
#   clamav-freshclam           installs fine, but needs the network for virus
#                              signatures. Fetch main.cvd, daily.cvd and
#                              bytecode.cvd from https://database.clamav.net/
#                              by hand and drop them in /var/lib/clamav/
#   *-dkms packages            need matching kernel headers in the bundle;
#                              linux-headers-generic is included above
# ===========================================================================
